column11: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

Wegovy is the closest comparator on five counts: the same class (GLP-1 receptor agonism), the same route and weekly interval, the same label (noncirrhotic MASH with F2 to F3 fibrosis, accelerated approval, DailyMed SPL ee06186f-2aa3-4990-a760-757579d8f77b published 30 June 2026; openFDA NDA215256 supplement 24, efficacy, priority, approved 2025-08-15), CMS itself lists MASH among Wegovy's uses, and semaglutide 2.4 mg is the active comparator arm of efinopegdutide's own Phase 2b (NCT05877547). The CMS figure halved is the book's incretin price basis (regn_olatorepatide.csv, abbv_abbv_295.csv); a Wegovy list price is not used because no measured gross-to-net pairs with it
column12: JUDGEMENT ON THE COMPARATOR AND THE LARGEST LEVER HERE. Rezdiffra, the other MASH seeds' comparator, nets $31,938.63 a patient-year (Q2 2026 net sales $364.3mm x 4 over the mean of more than 42,250 and more than 49,000 patients on therapy, Madrigal 8-Ks 0001628280-26-030896 and 0001628280-26-050775), 6.77x the $4,715.32 net here. The case for Rezdiffra: Merck develops efinopegdutide for MASH alone, and a liver-only label could carry a specialty price. The case against: payers can step through Wegovy, which already holds the same label at incretin prices, and semaglutide carries a Medicare negotiated price of $274 per 30 days from 2027 (negotiated_prices, cms_mfp). Merck reports in USD, so no conversion

column11: Rodriguez PJ et al., JAMA Netw Open 2025;8(1):e2457349, doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.57349 (PMID 39888616): 125,474 US adults with overweight or obesity starting semaglutide, liraglutide or tirzepatide, 2018 to 2023. One-year discontinuation was 46.5% with type 2 diabetes and 64.8% without; 76,524 (61.0%) had type 2 diabetes. Weighted by the cohort's own split: 0.609879 x 0.465 + 0.390121 x 0.648 = 0.536392
column12: the class rate, since efinopegdutide is a GLP-1 co-agonist and no persistence exists for it. The obesity seeds carry the 64.8% because their pool excludes diabetes; a MASH pool does not. Case for higher: the Phase 2a showed more gastrointestinal adverse events on efinopegdutide than on semaglutide 1 mg (Romero-Gomez M et al., J Hepatol 2023;79:888-897, PMID 37355043), and the same JAMA study finds moderate or severe gastrointestinal events raise the hazard of stopping (HR 1.19 to 1.38). Case for lower: biopsy-staged patients under specialist care. The penetration below is struck at this same rate, so the two move together

column11: judgement, since no Phase 3 is registered and Merck gives no timing: the Phase 2b (NCT05877547) completed 2025-12-29 and the compensated cirrhosis Phase 2 (NCT06465186) on 2026-08-03, with no Phase 3 study under efinopegdutide, MK-6024, HM12525A or JNJ-64565111 on the registry (clinicaltrials.gov API v2, read 2026-09-26), and Merck's chart as of 5 August 2026 still lists MK-6024 in Phase 2 (10-Q 0000310158-26-000212). So a Phase 3 start in 2027 at the earliest. The analogue is resmetirom, the one new molecule to reach the MASH market: its Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH (NCT03900429) started 2019-03-28, Rezdiffra was approved on 2024-03-14 (openFDA NDA217785, priority review) and 2025 was its first full year, six years. 2027 + 6 = 2033

Case for more: the only head-to-head in the class, 72.7% against 42.3% relative liver fat reduction at week 24 versus semaglutide 1 mg (J Hepatol 2023, PMID 37355043); Rezdiffra's capture was still rising, 48,636 starts a year in H1 2026 (49,000 at 30 June 2026, 8-K 0001628280-26-050775, less 36,250 x 0.463608^0.5 carried), 0.88% of the pool left.
